plugins.name: Woodwork
plugins.description: Cabinets and furniture in sheet goods: carcass generator and cut list.

release.notes:
Needs SolidCraft 0.49 or later (tested on 0.49.0).

## One Cabinet dialog for new and picked cabinets

Cabinet has a Mode: Auto (see below), New cabinet or Edit picked. Edit picked works on one cabinet: the dialog starts at that cabinet's own values (sizes from Parameters) and shows only the fields it takes, and nothing is built when nothing changed. The separate Edit cabinet function is gone. What is design-wide, such as joinery and the finger-joint options, is in Woodwork settings.

## Auto mode: new or edit from what you pick

Cabinet's Mode starts on Auto, which picks New or Edit from what is selected. Pick a door, drawer front, shelf, divider or drawer part, and Cabinet edits that cabinet. Pick a side, top, bottom or back and it makes a new cabinet next to that one; pick nothing for a new one on its own. The Mode hint says which it will do.

| Door picked: edits this cabinet | Side picked: a new cabinet next to it |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/auto-edit.png) | ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/auto-new.png) |

## A new settings system

Woodwork settings now hold the choices that are the same for the whole design: joinery, hardware, plinth, fronts, the cut list and more. "Show settings for" picks one section (General, Doors and fronts, Drawers, Plinth / toe kick and wall mount, Joinery, Cut list and worktop, Display, or All); Units is set in General. The fields start at what is stored, and Settings only stores.

| Show settings for: the sections | The Joinery section |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/settings-sections-crop.png) | ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/settings-joinery-crop.png) |

New cabinets take the settings. The Cabinet dialog, and Edit with it, now has only what belongs to one cabinet: sizes, doors, drawers, shelves, handles and the like.

**Apply settings** is a new function that builds the picked cabinets, or all of them, again with the current settings. It never overwrites what you chose for a single cabinet: sizes, doors and drawers stay. A per-cabinet choice such as handles follows the new setting only if it was left at the default. It runs as a long job, with progress per cabinet and a Cancel button, and has no 30 s run time limit.

| Before: board plinths | After Plinth type Legs in Settings, then Apply settings |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/apply-before.png) | ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/apply-after.png) |

![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/kitchen.png)

*Base cabinets on a plinth and wall cabinets without one: Plinth Yes or No is chosen per cabinet, its height and type come from the settings.*

## Finger joints

Finger joints for the cabinet shell (the top and bottom through to the outside), for corner cabinets, and for the drawer boxes (the front and back through), chosen in Woodwork settings with the finger width. Over a plinth the bottom stays a plain butt joint unless you choose otherwise.

| Shell and drawer boxes | A drawer box corner |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/finger-joints.png) | ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/finger-drawer.png) |

![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/finger-plinth.png)

*Over a plinth board: the top is finger-jointed, the bottom butted.*

![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/finger-corner.png)

*An L-shaped corner cabinet: the top and bottom finger-jointed to all four uprights.*

## Smaller changes

- Dialogs hide the fields that cannot combine with another choice, and the build ignores them.
- With Match selected, height, depth, thickness and plinth show greyed with the picked cabinet's values.
- Dialog hooks stay light with 30 or more cabinets, and placing a cabinet is faster in large designs (only the cabinets a run reads are measured; one pattern for a panel's pin rows).
- A cabinet sized by its drawers' inside keeps that inside: Edit and Apply settings (for example a new slide type) work its outside size out again, and Edit shows the inside sizes.
- Apply settings follows a changed default, and keeps what was chosen per cabinet.
- Clearer labels: "Plinth / toe kick", and "Dado runners" for the wooden runners.
- The plugin uses SolidCraft's plugin interface craft:plugin@0.2.0.

## Known issues and workarounds

- **Doors that share a divider** ([#157](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/issues/157)). With 3 overlay doors and 2 dividers, two doors meet on each divider and each covers only half of it. A door hinged on a divider then needs a half-overlay (cranked) hinge, which the model and the hardware list do not show yet. Workaround: use inset fronts, or buy half-overlay hinges for the doors hinged on a divider.

  ![](https://github.com/TomasDJo/solidcraft-woodwork/releases/download/v0.5.0/known-divider.png)

  *Seen from above: two doors meet on the divider, each covering half of it.*

- **Hardware models show under the first cabinet** (SolidCraft [#22153](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues/22153), fixed in SolidCraft by [#22274](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/pull/22274), in its next release). SolidCraft does not keep a plugin's hidden bodies, so the hinge and slide models the copies are made from show at the origin, under the first cabinet. Workaround: ignore them, they are not in the cut list.

  *Seen from below. The models are coloured orange here so they stand out; in SolidCraft they are grey.*

plugins.name: Gridfinity
plugins.description: Gridfinity bins (hollow, eco or solid), baseplates, and drawer baseplates split to fit your printer or a picked drawer floor, on a full, half or custom grid. Edit bin changes a bin it made, showing its settings.

release.notes:
**Needs SolidCraft 0.50.0 or newer.** For SolidCraft 0.49.1, use [1.7.0](https://github.com/tharje/gridfinity-solidcraft/releases/tag/v1.7.0).

## A grid on stackable lids (#13, thanks to sapstar)

A **Stackable** lid now has a baseplate's grid on top: a pocket over each cell, so the bins you put on it stand in place, as on a baseplate. The pockets stop 0.6 mm below a baseplate's top, so the lid's edge keeps a 0.4 mm wall (a lid is 0.5 mm narrower than a baseplate). A 3×2 lid takes 67.9 cm³.

![A stackable lid with a pocket over each cell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tharje/gridfinity-solidcraft/main/docs/images/lid-stackable-grid.png)

## Fewer buttons in the ribbon (#18, thanks to vilts)

The panel's ten helper commands (panel-refresh, quick-bin-…, layout-…, settings-change) no longer fill the Plugins group: they sit behind one **Panel helpers** button. They are for the Gridfinity panel; use the panel's buttons instead. SolidCraft can't hide them yet (tangency-labs/solidcraft#22060).

![The Panel helpers button and its menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tharje/gridfinity-solidcraft/main/docs/images/ribbon-panel-helpers.png)

## Install
Download `gridfinity-1.7.1.zip` below, then in SolidCraft: **Plugins › Install plugin…** and pick the zip. Or use **Open in SolidCraft** on the [Workshop](https://workshop.solidcraft.io/plugin/tharje/gridfinity).

plugins.name: SolidInserts
plugins.description: Create heat-set insert seats and embedded hex nut pockets in existing holes.

release.notes:
## Captive Nut Pockets

SolidInserts now creates internal pockets for **DIN 934 hex nuts** that you insert during a print pause. **Insert Seats** remains available for heat-set inserts. The same ZIP works without patches on official SolidCraft Desktop **0.46.2** and **0.48.1**. Compatibility with 0.48.1 was verified on Linux.

- Select the hole rims and the face that rests on the print bed. Automatic sizing picks the nearest nominal nut size for each hole within **±0.25 mm**. A Ø3 mm hole selects M3. Use manual sizing for ties or diameters outside that range.
- **Pause heights (mm)** estimates where to pause with fixed layers, including a different first-layer height. For adaptive layers, set **Layer height** to **0** to see the geometric height at which each pocket closes.
- **Send to Slicer** reuses the print face saved when you apply the pockets. Add the pauses in the slicer after checking its layer preview.

## Italiano

**Captive Nut Pockets** crea tasche interne per dadi esagonali DIN 934 da inserire durante una pausa di stampa. **Insert Seats** resta disponibile per gli inserti a caldo. Lo stesso ZIP funziona senza patch su SolidCraft Desktop **0.46.2** e **0.48.1** ufficiali. La compatibilità con la 0.48.1 è stata verificata su Linux.

- La misura automatica sceglie per ciascun foro il diametro nominale più vicino entro **±0,25 mm**. Un foro Ø3 mm seleziona M3. Scegli la misura manualmente se due diametri sono equidistanti o se il foro è fuori soglia.
- **Pause heights (mm)** stima le quote di pausa per layer fissi, anche con un primo layer di altezza diversa. Per i layer adattivi, imposta **Layer height** a **0** per vedere la quota geometrica di chiusura di ogni tasca.
- **Send to Slicer** riusa la faccia di stampa salvata quando applichi le tasche. Controlla l’anteprima dei layer nello slicer e aggiungi lì le pause.

Install `solidinserts-1.3.1.zip` from **File → Plugins…**. The `.zip.sha256` file contains the ZIP's SHA-256 checksum.

plugins.name: Bearings
plugins.description: Insert radial bearings and CSK one-way clutches.

release.notes:
All six plugins now share internal part definitions and verified component reuse.
Bearings and V-wheels add supplier products with visible exterior detail. The Bearing dialog also offers a supplier-neutral sealed 105.
CSK clutches add customizable exterior geometry with reference sources recorded
separately.

## Bearings and V-wheels

- **Bearings** offers base size and closure or a search by nominal bore, outside diameter and width. Thirteen closed variants use estimated exteriors. Twelve carry catalog-confirmed MISUMI numbers, and the sealed 105 has a supplier-neutral BOM row. Open remains available for 626. The [product table](../plugins/techsquid-bearings/README.md#supported-bearings-and-csk-presets) lists each exterior basis.
- **V-wheels** offers Solid, Xtreme Solid, grooved Delrin, Delrin Mini and Xtreme Mini products. Choose a bare wheel or a core comprising one wheel, two bearings and one internal shim.
- Direct bearings and wheel assemblies reuse the same verified bearing definition. The wheel package contains its dependencies; installing Bearings separately is optional.
- Core assemblies list their separate purchases in the BOM. They are not retail kits and do not include mounting axles, external spacers, washers or nuts.
- Geometry is built from native features using measured STEP profiles. Source hashes, dimensional discrepancies and the 105ZZ correction from 4.2 to 4 mm are documented. Original STEP files are not distributed.

Bearing closures are intentional zero-thickness surface bodies; rings are exterior
envelopes. These models support layout and appearance, not physical bearing mass,
internal contact or manufacturing sections. Metal wheels and the supplied inch and
8 × 16 × 5 bearings remain unpublished candidates pending exact product evidence.

## Bearings dialogs

The Bearings submenu has four commands. **Bearing** inserts a radial preset. **CSK clutch** inserts or edits a preset, or starts from scratch. It shows the inherited closure next to each starting preset. **Bearing by dimensions** and **CSK clutch by dimensions** share the numeric millimetre controls for nominal bore, outside diameter and width. See the [Bearings reference](../plugins/techsquid-bearings/REFERENCE.md).

## Customizable CSK clutches

- Reference publishers such as Formsprag are not assigned manufacturers. CSK specifications have no purchase identity or BOM part number. Purchasing assignment is [future work for a shared component workflow](../docs/parts-library.md#future-component-purchasing-workflow) after creation.
- Custom and unsourced parts remain countable in the BOM. Repeated identical geometry reuses a definition; different keyway values stay separate.
- Each component contains two chamfered solid rings and two cover/seal faces, with full-width rectangular keyways. Eight supplied STEP files establish measured exterior sections; other variants use explicitly recorded estimates. PP keyways default to opposing sides. Hidden sprags, raceways, seal cross-sections, rotation simulation and mass predictions remain outside the representation. Torque and load ratings are source-specific selection information, not geometry parameters.

See the [CSK example](../examples/bearings-and-clutches/#csk-references-and-overrides) and [source ledger](../docs/sources/csk.md).

## Nylon-insert lock nuts

The Hex nut dialog adds thin DIN 985 nylon-insert lock nuts. Choose the style and size to create a loose nut, a flush captive pocket, or both. The [V-slot gantry](../examples/v-slot-gantry/) uses four M5 lock nuts.

New custom nut descriptions include thread size, pitch, width across flats and height.

**BOM change for near-diameter inputs.** New insertions of `M5.0000001x0.8` and `M5` now share the nominal M5 part number. Existing saved definitions keep their original part numbers and descriptions. To consolidate a duplicate row in a saved design, replace its occurrences with the nominal size.

If Hex nuts is already installed, install the updated ZIP through **Preferences → Plugins** and review the replacement. SolidCraft ties plugin approvals to the exact package.

**Breaking change for installed-tool calls.** Scripts calling `techsquid-nuts.make-nut` must pass `style`. Add `"style": "Plain hex"` to keep creating plain nuts. Existing `plugin.run` recipes default to Plain hex.

## Extrusions and slot nuts

- **Slot nuts come in M3, M4 and M5.** Size picks the thread of the MISUMI pre-assembly (HNTT5) or post-assembly (HNTP5) nut. The outer shape stays the same within each type; the tapped hole and the part number change.
- **The Extrusion dialog starts with Mode**, then Slot, Size and Length. Holes from is now **Hole face** and Hole distances from is now **Measure holes from**; the keys `hole_face` and `holes_from` are unchanged.

## One parts-library foundation

Nut-pocket batches and repeated runs now reserve distinct names for their planes,
profiles, cuts and bolt holes. Existing names in other components, case variants
and numbered suffixes are respected, including after reopening a saved design.
Renaming a part and all its bodies no longer lets a replacement collide with the
original sketches. Face-attached pocket layouts preserve the selected copied or
nested assembly through consecutive insertions; hardware seat joints identify
that exact placement.

Packages expose insertion tools only. The shared internal descriptors retain
dimensions, provenance, attachment frames, configuration rules and assembly
members. Catalog discovery is deferred: the host currently displays every entry
as a command but cannot provide a useful Catalog form. No Catalog buttons or
public query handlers are shipped.

Product identity is separate from CAD detail, placement and display names.

release.notes:
Woodworking joints for SolidCraft, as a command plugin. In this version you pick the boards with a click, a docked *Joints* panel lists the joints of the design, and the French package speaks French. It is made for SolidCraft 0.51.

## Install

You need the SolidCraft desktop application, **version 0.51.0 or later**. On 0.50 everything works but opening a joint's form from the Joints panel. On SolidCraft 0.46 to 0.49, install [v0.13.0](https://github.com/WilliamHJKL/solidcraft-wood-joinery/releases/tag/v0.13.0) instead.

1. Download `wood-joinery-en.zip` (English) or `wood-joinery-fr.zip` (French) below. Do not take the "Source code" archives, and do not unzip the file.
2. In SolidCraft, open Preferences › Plugins. If an older version is installed, click Remove on its card first.
3. Click Install plugin… and pick the file. The plugin asks for the same commands as 0.14.0, and for one more capability, `ui`, for the Joints panel.

Install one package only. Both have the same plugin id. Your designs keep their joints, and Edit a joint and Update joints read the joints made with older versions.

## New

- **Pick the boards with a click.** The board fields of the thirteen joints work like Extrude's *Profiles*: the first one is active when the form opens, a click on a board in the view or in the browser fills it, and the next field takes the next click. Each field shows the board's name and a cross to empty it. Boards selected before you open the form still fill it.
- **The Joints panel.** Docked on the right, it lists the joints of the open design with their state, and says whether the boards changed since the last update. *Update joints* and *Refresh* are its buttons; a double click on a row opens that joint's form (SolidCraft 0.51). SolidCraft does not yet tell a panel when a design opens (tangency-labs/solidcraft#21824): press *Refresh* to fill the list.
- **Messages in French.** The French package gives its warnings and refusals in French, with a decimal comma: "la mortaise laisse une joue de 6,0 mm dans le montant…". The names of the joints' folders stay in English, as the designs keep them.

## Fixed

- **Edit a joint applies at the first click.** Apply no longer asks to check the form and to be pressed again: opening the form changes nothing in the design. The form shows, greyed at its foot, the joint it replaces.

## Changed, for scripts

A board is now given as a list of one name, `{"rail": ["Rail"], "stile": ["Stile"]}`, or as the reference a click sends, `[{"type": "body", "name": "Rail"}]`. SolidCraft refuses a plain name. Leaving the boards out and selecting them first with `select.set` still works.

Joints, sizes and results are the same as in 0.14.0.

## Tested

On SolidCraft 0.51.1 and 0.50.0: 96 unit tests, 208 end-to-end checks and 13 joints in 12 orientations each, from the command line. In the 0.51.1 app: a mortise and tenon picked with two clicks (one in the browser, one in the view) and made at the first Run, the Joints panel in French with its Refresh button, and a double click on its row opening the joint's form, filled, which replaced the joint at the first click.

- NIST: **0 of 19 exact matches**, 12 fully decoded rebuild attempts and 7 reader-blocked parts.
  This is unchanged in success rate; imported-solid fallbacks are not counted.
- Private release sample: **6 of 40 exact rebuilds**, no losses, crashes or memory-limit events.
  Only this aggregate is public; names, paths, geometry and per-file results remain local.
- **120 Python tests pass (5 skipped); all 19 Rust tests pass.** Python/Rust parity is zero
  differences on 54 public files and 43 designs. Checks used SolidCraft CLI 0.50.0.
- See `logs/survey-0.18.0.md` for the measured release summary. The remaining long private scan is
  diagnostic work and is not needed to validate this release.

### Added
- `tools/process_limit.py` adds a watchdog that checks working-set memory and terminates a
  conversion and its process tree if `--memory-mb` is exceeded (default 8192 MiB). Timeout and
  memory-limit results include the reason; large output is drained without deadlocking the watcher.
- `tools/convert_sample.py` accepts a whole folder as well as a list, skips lock files, and takes
  `--timeout` for long per-part conversion runs. JSONL results are flushed after every part and

  memory pressure; ordinary files keep the selected `--jobs` count.

plugins.name: Mesh Solidify
plugins.description: Rebuild a broken mesh body (holes, open shells, overlaps) as one watertight, printable solid. Adds the result as a new body.

release.notes:
Rewritten in Rust, primarily as a **SolidCraft plugin**, with a standalone command line that needs no Python.

## Assets

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `mesh-solidify-plugin.zip` | SolidCraft plugin (0.41+). Preferences › Plugins › Install plugin…, then Plugins › Mesh Solidify. |
| `mesh-solidify-v0.2.0-<target>.tar.gz` / `.zip` | Command line for macOS (Apple Silicon, Intel), Linux (x86-64, ARM64) and Windows. |
| `mesh-solidify-skill.zip` | Claude Code skill. Unzip into `.claude/skills/`. |
| `solidify.py` | The original Python version (0.1.1), for reference. |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums. |

## Highlights

- **Plugin:** *Solidify Mesh…* rebuilds the selected mesh body as a new watertight body in one undo step. The dialog defaults to 10% scale. *Inspect Mesh…* reports holes, loose parts and size.
- **CLI:** same flags, `--json` and exit codes as 0.1; about 2× faster with a quarter of the memory (978k-triangle compressor: 35 s instead of 76 s; 650k-triangle toolbox at 400M voxels: 34 s and 2 GB instead of 123 s and 7.8 GB). New `--voxel auto` and `--threads`; reads PLY.
- Octree winding-number evaluation, marching tetrahedra, manifold-preserving decimation, void filling.

## SolidCraft 0.41.0 limits

These are the host's limits, not the plugin's:
- A plugin can read mesh bodies of at most **2,730 triangles**, and send back about 30,000. For larger scans use the CLI and *Insert Mesh*.
- **macOS:** the signed 0.41.0 build lacks the JIT entitlement Wasmtime needs, so running *any* plugin kills the process ("Code Signature Invalid"). Use a build without the hardened runtime until SolidCraft fixes it.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/JakeMathews/mesh-solidify/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

release.notes:
Thread Generator for [SolidCraft](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft): 3D-printable threads with clearance, cut into the face you select in SolidCraft.

## New in 1.8.0

- **One Size field.** The separate Diameter and Pitch fields are gone, so the size you see is the size that's cut. Pick from the list or type your own, like `M9x1.5`.
- **1 mm pitch on every size** from M4 to M50 (M8x1, M10x1, …), next to 2, 2.5, 3.5 and 5 mm.
- When you use a new face, the **pitch you picked is kept** and the diameter follows the face.
- **New defaults:** M8x1, tolerance O.15, height 85%.

## Install

1. Download **thread-generator-1.8.0.zip** below.
2. In SolidCraft open **Preferences → Plugins → Show in folder** and unzip it there, so you get `plugins\thread-generator\plugin.json`. Updating? Close Thread Generator first and replace the old folder.
3. Start **ThreadGenerator.exe** from that folder. Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" because the program isn't code-signed: click *More info → Run anyway*.

Needs Windows 10/11 and SolidCraft 0.22 or later for threading a face. No Python needed.

## What it does

- **Thread a face in SolidCraft:** select a shaft or the inside of a hole, pick a size, tolerance and height, and SolidCraft cuts a modeled thread into it.
- **3D-printed metric sizes** after [CustomThreads](https://github.com/BalzGuenat/CustomThreads): 1, 2 (experimental), 2.5, 3.5 and 5 mm pitches, plus ISO metric, fine and UNC.
- **Tolerance classes** O.0, O.1, O.15, O.2, O.4, O.8 and **height** 70–100%: lower teeth with flat tops that still fit a matching nut.
- A to-scale **drawing** of bolt and nut that explains each setting.
- **Export repaired 3MF:** exports the selected body and runs Windows' own model repair on it, then opens it in your slicer.
- **Make parts (STL):** bolts, nuts, threaded rods and thread cutters as watertight STL.
- Follows SolidCraft's light or dark theme.

- Three MCP tools: `codemode.run {code}` runs a JavaScript script in the open design as one undo step,

plugins.name: OmiGears
plugins.description: Gears, gear pairs and gearboxes, each part a component: involute, bevel, worm, planetary and cycloidal gears, timing pulleys, sprockets, ratchets and Geneva drives, with bores, hubs and fits for 3D printing.

release.notes:
OmiGears 0.50.3 is a rebuild. Every gear is now a component, pairs and sets come joined so that they turn together, and every form has a fit for 3D printing and a choice of bores. It adds whole gearboxes (planetary, compound gear train, cycloidal), timing pulleys, chain sprockets, a ratchet and a Geneva drive. Bevel gears, wrong until now, are right.

## Install

1. With OmiGears 0.50.1 or 0.50.2 installed, take the update SolidCraft offers on its card in **Preferences › Plugins**. Otherwise download **omigears-0.50.3.zip** below.
2. In SolidCraft (desktop): **Preferences › Plugins › Install plugin…** and pick the zip. The review lists the modelling commands it uses, which now include components, placements and joints. It asks for no file or network access.

**Requires SolidCraft 0.50.0 or later.**

## New

- **Every part is a component.** A gear is no longer drawn into the design itself: it is a component with one body, drawn about its own origin and put in place by its placement. Move it, copy it or join it as any other component. Equal parts are placements of one component: a planetary set's planets, a gear train's compound gears.
- **Pairs, in mesh and joined.** Spur, helical and herringbone gears take **Mating gear's teeth**; bevel and cycloidal gears build their mate by default; a worm takes its wheel, an internal gear its pinion. Each gear turns on a revolute joint and the joints are coupled with the pair's ratio: drive one and the other follows.
- **Made by: 3D printing.** The default fit takes 0.1 mm off each tooth and adds 0.2 mm to each bore, so a printed pair runs and a printed bore takes its shaft. **Machining** draws the nominal size; **Custom** shows both numbers. A printed gear's reply says when its teeth are too fine for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
- **Bores:** round, D, double D, hexagon, square, or round with a DIN 6885 keyway, and a **hub** round them. A D bore's flat is where motor shafts have it: a 5 mm bore fits a NEMA 17.
- **Planetary gearbox:** ring housing, sun, planets and carriers for one to four stages in one ring, with an output shaft that is round, D, hexagonal or square. 5:1, 25:1, 125:1 with the defaults.
- **Gear train:** a compound spur reducer of one to six stages on two shafts, between two plates.
- **Cycloidal reducer:** housing, disc, eccentric input and output plate, coupled so that driving the eccentric shows the motion.
- **Timing pulley:** GT2 (2, 3 and 5 mm), HTD (3M, 5M, 8M), T2.5, T5, T10, MXL and XL, with flanges that print without support.
- **Chain sprocket:** the ISO 606 tooth form for 04B to 12B, ANSI 25 to 60, bicycle chains or a custom chain.
- **Ratchet and pawl**, and **Geneva drive** of 3 to 24 slots.
- **Two buttons:** **Gears** for gears and pairs, **Gear drives** for sets, gearboxes and mechanisms.
- **Root fillets by default** (0.3 × module), clamped to the largest that fits the tooth space.

## Fixed

- **Bevel teeth were too shallow.** OmiGears 0.50.2 and earlier left bevel teeth cos²δ of their depth (δ is the pitch angle): a miter gear had half, and a 30-tooth gear for a 10-tooth mate a tenth, so it looked like a flat disc. The teeth are now spherical involutes of full depth at the heel, on a turned blank with a back cone, a front cone and a flat back face. Hypoid members get the same teeth and blank.
- **Edit gear moves a sketch to its new plane.** A herringbone made thicker failed, and a gear edited onto another plane stayed where it was.
- **A ring gear's tips fouled its pinion** on small tooth differences: with the pinion known, the ring's tips are kept clear of its flanks.
- **A shifted pair lost its root clearance:** both gears' tips are now shortened by what the centre distance grows less than the shift.
- **A cycloidal drive's housing wall could cut into the disc's lobes** between the pins.
- **Worm wheels for steep worms** fouled the worm's root: lead angles over 30° are refused, under **Starts**.
- **A root fillet too large for the tooth space** was refused; it is now drawn as large as fits.
- **Undercut advice could not always be followed:** the profile shift it named could point the teeth. It now names one that leaves a tip, and warns of tips under 0.2 × module.
- **An edit by script lost the inputs it did not name.** `{"teeth": 24, "op": "1"}` now keeps the gear's other inputs. An `op` that names no gear is refused instead of making a new one.
- **Editing the first of two equal gears renamed it** "… (3)".

## Faster and lighter

Flanks are smooth curves through a few points, with true arcs for tips, roots and fillets, and each sketch reaches SolidCraft in one command. A 20-tooth spur has 123 faces where it had 403; a 60-tooth helical gear sweeps in 3.2 s where it took 6.8 s. **Points per flank** is gone: there is nothing left to tune.

## Editing

- **Edit gear works on pairs, sets and gearboxes.** Pick any body. A part that keeps its steps changes in place; one that takes other steps is rebuilt in its own component; a mate or a stage asked for is added, one left out is deleted.
- **A gear stays where you put it.** Move a pair, then change its mate's teeth: the mate lands in mesh where the pair is.
- **Joints are made again and turned as far as they were.**

## Changes to note

- **Scripts:** `flank_points` and `lobe_points` are gone. The rack's `pinion_bore` is `bore`. The cycloidal gear's `build` is the flag `mate`. `bevel` builds its mate unless `mate` is false. A hidden input (one whose field does not show for the other inputs) is not read.
- **Defaults changed:** fit is 3D printing (backlash 0.1 mm, bore clearance 0.2 mm) and roots are filleted, so default volumes differ. `"fit": "exact", "root_fillet": 0` gives the old gear.
- **Gears made by OmiGears 0.50.2** are rebuilt as components by their first edit. Their form opens with what their inputs meant: custom fit with their own backlash, sharp roots, no joints.
- **Joints** are made only when the parts go into the design itself, since a joint holds a part to the desi

plugins.description: Evolventen-Zahnräder: Einzelräder und Getriebepaare: Stirnrad (gerade, schräg, Pfeil), Hohlrad, Zahnstange, Schnecke, Schneckenrad, Kegelrad (90°), Kronenrad.

release.notes:
## Zahnrad-Generator 1.4.0

**English:** Open-source (MIT) plugin for [SolidCraft](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft) that generates involute gears and gear sets as ordinary, editable solids. Tested with SolidCraft 0.46.2. The user interface is German.

### New in 1.4.0
- **Joints and motion simulation built in:** every gear is built as its own component. The plugin adds revolute joints (a slider joint for the rack), the gear coupling with the correct ratio and a drive motion study, so you can simulate the motion right away. Can be switched off with the option "Drehgelenke + Kopplung einbauen" (build joints + coupling).
- **Crown gear with exact flank** (envelope of the pinion's involute profile); face width 0 = automatic.
- **Body names include tooth count, module and ratio**, e.g. "Ritzel Z15 m2" (pinion), "Rad Z45 m2 (i=3)" (wheel).
- **Gearbox:** the ratio i accumulates per stage, i = Z2/Z1 · Z4/Z3 · … (pitch circles, not tip circles).

### Included
Spur gear, internal gear, rack, worm and worm wheel, bevel gear, crown gear, matching gear pairs and multi-stage gearboxes.

### Installation
Download `zahnrad-1.4.0.zip`, unpack it and put the folder into SolidCraft's plugin folder (Preferences → Plugins → *Show in folder*), then install and approve the plugin there. A plugin runs Wasm code, so review the source first.

### Known limits
For the internal gear, the worm and the gearbox stage Z10/Z50 the collision check still reports 0.03–0.1 mm of contact that SolidCraft could not measure. The bevel gear is a geometric approximation. At most about 64 host calls per run (gearbox: field "Ab Stufe" to continue).

---

**Deutsch:** Open-Source-Plugin (MIT) für [SolidCraft](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft): Evolventen-Zahnräder und Getriebe als normale, editierbare Volumenkörper. Getestet mit SolidCraft 0.46.2.

### Neu in 1.4.0
- **Drehgelenke und Simulation direkt im Plugin:** Jedes Zahnrad wird als eigene Komponente gebaut. Das Plugin legt Drehgelenke (bei der Zahnstange ein Schiebegelenk), die Getriebekopplung mit dem richtigen Übersetzungsverhältnis und eine Antriebsstudie an. Die Bewegung lässt sich sofort simulieren. Abschaltbar über „Drehgelenke + Kopplung einbauen".
- **Kronenrad mit exakter Flanke** (Hüllkurve des Ritzel-Evolventenprofils), Zahnbreite 0 = automatisch.
- **Körpernamen mit Zähnezahl, Modul und Übersetzung**, z. B. „Ritzel Z15 m2", „Rad Z45 m2 (i=3)".
- **Getriebe:** Übersetzung i läuft pro Stufe auf, i = Z2/Z1 · Z4/Z3 · … (Teilkreise, nicht Kopfkreise).

### Enthalten
Stirnrad, Hohlrad, Zahnstange, Schnecke und Schneckenrad, Kegelrad, Kronenrad, Paarungen mit passendem Gegenstück und mehrstufige Getriebe.

### Installation
`zahnrad-1.4.0.zip` herunterladen, entpacken und den Ordner in den Plugin-Ordner von SolidCraft legen (Einstellungen → Plugins → *Im Ordner zeigen*), dann dort installieren und freigeben. Ein Plugin führt Wasm-Code aus: vorher den Quelltext prüfen.

### Bekannte Grenzen
Bei Hohlrad, Schnecke und der Getriebestufe Z10/Z50 meldet die Kollisionsprüfung noch 0,03–0,1 mm Berührung, die SolidCraft nicht ausmessen konnte. Das Kegelrad ist eine geometrische Näherung. Pro Lauf höchstens etwa 64 Aufrufe (Getriebe: Feld „Ab Stufe").

release.notes:
# Зубчатые передачи 0.10.10

В SolidCraft 0.51.2 проверены предпросмотр всех 13 команд и 27 построений с исходными и изменёнными параметрами. В каждом построении получено ожидаемое число замкнутых тел с положительным объёмом.

| Команда | Тел при исходных настройках | Дополнительная проверка |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Прямозубое колесо | 1 | Задание по двум роликам, бочкообразность зубьев |
| Косозубое колесо | 1 | Задание по делительному диаметру, левый зуб, плоскость YZ |
| Шевронное колесо | 1 | Отверстие, плоскость XZ, левое направление первой половины |
| Колесо с внутренними зубьями | 1 | Пересчёт зацепления с указанной шестернёй |
| Коническое колесо | 1 | Пример 15/30 зубьев из приложения 4 ГОСТ 19624-74 |
| Гипоидная передача | 1 | Поочерёдное построение колеса и шестерни |
| Червяк | 1 | Многовитковое тело, левый двухзаходный червяк со сквозным отверстием |
| Червячное колесо | 1 | Двухзаходный левый червяк в исходных данных |
| Зубчатая рейка | 2 | Построение отдельно и с шестернёй |
| Планетарная передача | 5 | Два сочетания чисел зубьев и модуля |
| Циклоидальные колёса | 2 | Построение отдельно и в паре |
| Циклоидальный редуктор | 2 | Диск без выходных отверстий и с одним отверстием |
| Зубчатая пара | 2 | Нечётные числа зубьев, разные отверстия |

В формах доступно 139 расчётных полей. Набор видимых величин зависит от команды и способа задания. Для рейки и гипоидной пары вынесены размеры сопряжённых деталей. Для редуктора с выходными пальцами выводятся диаметр и окружность размещения отверстий. Размеры в форме и при построении рассчитываются из одних исходных данных.

Червяк строится одной винтовой операцией. Для предпросмотра шевронного колеса показываются обе половины венца, а при завершении команды SolidCraft объединяет их в одно тело. Такое объединение на исходных настройках заняло около двух минут.

Для планетарной передачи начальное утонение зуба составляет 0,03 мм на колесо. У циклоидального редуктора появился отдельный нормальный зазор между диском и цевкой, исходное значение 0,03 мм. Оба значения можно менять. При нуле форма предупреждает о возможном пересечении аппроксимированных профилей. В исходном положении всех пяти многотельных сборок SolidCraft не обнаружил объёмных пересечений при начальных настройках. Проверка относится к этому положению сборок.

Основные геометрические зависимости наружного и внутреннего цилиндрического зацеплений сверены с [ГОСТ 16532-70](https://allgosts.ru/21/200/gost_16532-70) и [ГОСТ 19274-73](https://allgosts.ru/21/200/gost_19274-73). Средние и внутренние размеры прямозубого конического колеса проверены по числовому примеру приложения 4 [ГОСТ 19624-74](https://allgosts.ru/21/200/gost_19624-74). Делительные диаметры, угол подъёма и межосевое расстояние червячной передачи без смещения сверены с [ГОСТ 19650-74](https://allgosts.ru/21/200/gost_19650-74).

Червячное колесо имеет цилиндрический венец без огибающей впадины. Гипоидная геометрия приближённая. Для циклоидальных моделей проверены геометрия и построение по профилям генератора. Расчёт прочности, допуски на изготовление и проверка контакта за полный оборот выходят за пределы этой проверки.
